questions.passage: Psychologists Samantha Cohen and Peter Todd analyzed nationally representative data collected by the Centers for Disease Control to gain insight into the exploration-exploitation trade-off in real marital decisions. They learned that some people spend a long time dating several people before getting married, whereas others spend a short time dating a few and settle down quickly. In explore-exploit trade-off terminology, the first group explored for a long time before exploiting, whereas the second group explored for a short period before exploiting.

questions.passage: The animal behavior literature and computer simulations both suggest that insufficient exploration results in more errors. Of course, if one mate were far better than the rest, there would be no need to explore—the choice would be obvious. But in a real mating context, there are many potential mates with only slight differences in overall value. This means that it is better to explore more before settling down on one mate.
questions.prompt: Why does the passage argue for more exploration in the real mating context?
options: Many potential partners differ only slightly, unlike a case with one obviously superior choice.
One partner is assumed to be overwhelmingly better in every real situation.
Computer simulations are said to prove all marriages have identical outcomes.
Exploration is claimed to have no cost under any circumstances.

探索在任何情况下都无成本。
analyses: A if one...far better 的例外，与 But...many...slight differences 的现实描述形成论证。
B 把反事实条件例外当成所有现实。
C 模型错误率不等于所有婚姻结果一致。
D 前文已讨论成本，本片段没有否认成本。当前是模型与动物文献引出的推论，不把尚未在本片段出现的CDC结果倒灌成因果证明。

questions.passage: The CDC data indicates that those who spend less time exploring (those who get married quickly after starting a serious relationship) are indeed more likely to end their marriage in divorce than those who spend more time exploring before marriage. So, on average, the more exploration, the more marital stability.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion is supported by the CDC data as described?
options: Longer exploration guarantees that a marriage will last.
Shorter exploration is associated with a greater likelihood of divorce.
Divorce causes couples to shorten their premarital exploration.
Every long exploration ends in marriage.
questions.promptZh: 按片段描述，CDC 数据支持哪项结论？
optionsZh: 探索久保证婚姻持续。
探索较短与更高离婚可能性相关。
离婚导致婚前探索缩短。
每次长期探索都以婚姻告终。
analyses: A on average 是平均趋势，不能保证个体结果。
B more likely 明示两组离婚可能性的比较；观察性数据不能单独证明因果。
C 颠倒时间和论证方向，原文没有检验反向因果。
D 数据讨论已婚者的稳定性，没有追踪每次探索是否结婚。

evidence.quote: more likely to end their marriage in divorce than those who spend more time exploring before marriage.

vocabulary.context: 指婚姻维持的平均趋势，不是个人必然结果
vocabulary.example: The survey examined marital stability over time.

questions.translation: CDC 数据表明，花较少时间探索的人（开始认真交往后很快结婚的人），确实比婚前花更多时间探索的人更可能以离婚结束婚姻。因此，平均而言，探索越多，婚姻越稳定。

使对规则的一切批评都不可能。
说数据直接来自随机分派37%约会的任务。
所述模式与规则相容，但不单独证明每项精确处方。

B However 后正介绍质疑。
C 资料为观察性婚姻数据，不是分派的实验比例。
D 相容与完全证成不同，不能让宽泛平均关联替代模型所有条件的验证。

Treating exactly ten candidates as the whole pool regardless of its size.
